messages.content: "Can you help me with a couple of conversions? First, I have 5000 Euros that I want to convert into US Dollars using the latest exchange rate. Then, I have another 3000 Euros that I want to convert into British Pounds, but this time, I want to use the last known exchange rate. After that, I have a distance of 100 kilometers that I want to convert into miles. Lastly, I have a weight of 75 kilograms that I want to convert into pounds. Can you do these conversions for me?"

function.name: unit_conversion_convert
function.description: Converts a value from one unit to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: currency_exchange_convert
function.description: Converts a value from one currency to another using the latest exchange rate. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

amount.description: The amount of money to be converted.

live_conversion.description: If true, use the latest exchange rate for conversion, else use the last known rate. Default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user wants multiple conversions:

1) Convert 5,000 euros to USD using live/latest rates.

2) Convert 3,000 euros to GBP using last known (not live). So set live_conversion false or omitted default maybe true; we need to specify false.

3) Convert 100 km to miles.

4) Convert 75 kg to lbs.

We should call two different tool types: currency_exchange_convert and unit_conversion_convert.

We'll produce separate calls per conversion. We can combine them sequentially. We'll output results after each call.

Let's plan:

Call currency_exchange_convert twice:
First: {amount: 5000, from_currency:"EUR", to_currency:"USD"} -> default live_conversion True.

Second: {amount: 3000, from_currency:"EUR", to_currency:"GBP", live_conversion:false}

Then unit_conversion_convert twice:
Third: {value:100, from_unit:"kilometer", to_unit:"mile"}

Fourth: {value:75, from_unit:"kg", to_unit:"lb"} or "pound".

Need correct units names accepted by library. Usually "km" vs "miles". Let's assume "kilometers" and "miles" etc. Use standard abbreviations: "km" to "mi"; "kg" to "lb".

But better to provide full words: "kilometer" to "mile", "kilogram" to "pound".

Ok.

Return JSON responses accordingly.

Will produce four calls.
